On Friday, November 22, 1963, [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy"), the 35th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"), was [assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassinated "Assassinated") while riding in a presidential [motorcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcade "Motorcade") through [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza") in [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), Texas. Kennedy was in the vehicle with First Lady [Jacqueline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy "Jacqueline Kennedy"), Texas governor [John Connally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Connally "John Connally"), and Connally's wife [Nellie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Connally "Nellie Connally"), when he was fatally shot from the nearby [Texas School Book Depository](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_School_Book_Depository "Texas School Book Depository") by [Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald"), a former [U.S. Marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). The motorcade rushed to [Parkland Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_Memorial_Hospital "Parkland Memorial Hospital"), where Kennedy was pronounced dead about 30 minutes after the shooting; Connally was also wounded in the attack but recovered. Vice President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") was [hastily sworn in as president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson "First inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson") two hours and eight minutes later aboard [Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_One "Air Force One") at [Dallas Love Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Love_Field "Dallas Love Field").

After the assassination, Oswald returned home to retrieve a pistol; he shot and killed a lone Dallas policeman [J. D. Tippit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._D._Tippit "J. D. Tippit") shortly afterwards. Around 70 minutes after Kennedy and Connally were shot, Oswald was apprehended by the [Dallas Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Police_Department "Dallas Police Department") and charged under Texas state law with the murders of Kennedy and Tippit. Two days later, as live television cameras covered Oswald being moved through the basement of [Dallas Police Headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Municipal_Building "Dallas Municipal Building"), he was fatally shot by Dallas nightclub operator [Jack Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ruby "Jack Ruby"). Like Kennedy, Oswald was taken to Parkland Memorial Hospital, where he soon died. Ruby was convicted of Oswald's murder, though the decision was overturned on appeal, and Ruby died in prison in 1967 while awaiting a new trial.

After a 10-month investigation, the [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission") concluded that Oswald assassinated Kennedy, and that there was no evidence that either Oswald or Ruby was [part of a conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_conspiracy_theories "John F. Kennedy assassination conspiracy theories"). In 1967, New Orleans district attorney [Jim Garrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Garrison "Jim Garrison") brought the only [trial for Kennedy's murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Clay_Shaw "Trial of Clay Shaw") against businessman [Clay Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Shaw "Clay Shaw"); Shaw was acquitted. Subsequent federal investigations—such as the [Rockefeller Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Commission "Rockefeller Commission") and [Church Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Committee "Church Committee")—agreed with the Warren Commission's general findings. In its 1979 report, the [United States House Select Committee on Assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Assassinations "United States House Select Committee on Assassinations") (HSCA) concluded that Kennedy was likely "assassinated as a result of a conspiracy". The HSCA did not identify possible conspirators, but concluded that there was "a high probability that two gunmen fired at [the] President". The HSCA's conclusions were largely based on a [police Dictabelt recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_Dictabelt_recording "John F. Kennedy assassination Dictabelt recording"), which was subsequently debunked by the [U.S. Justice Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Justice_Department "U.S. Justice Department").

Kennedy's assassination is still the subject of widespread debate and has spawned many [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theories "Conspiracy theories") and alternative scenarios; polls have found that a vast majority of Americans believe there was a conspiracy. The assassination left a profound impact and was the first of four [major assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960s#Assassinations_and_attempts "1960s") during the [1960s in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960s_in_the_United_States "1960s in the United States"), coming two years before the [assassination of Malcolm X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Malcolm_X "Assassination of Malcolm X") in 1965, and five years before the assassinations of [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.") and Kennedy's brother [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Robert_F._Kennedy "Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy") in 1968. Kennedy was the fourth U.S. president to be assassinated and is the most recent to have [died in office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_who_died_in_office "List of presidents of the United States who died in office").

## Background

### Kennedy

Further information: [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") and [Presidency of John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy "Presidency of John F. Kennedy")

[![Image 7: President Kennedy is pictured speaking behind a podium. Rice University's stadium is visible behind him.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg/250px-John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg)

[Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") delivering his "[We choose to go to the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon "We choose to go to the Moon")" speech at [Rice University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_University "Rice University"), 1962

In 1960, John F. Kennedy, then a [U.S. senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"), was elected the 35th president of the United States with [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") as his vice president.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bugliosixi-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-4) Kennedy's tenure saw the height of the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and much of his foreign policy was dedicated to countering the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and [communism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-6) As president, he authorized operations to overthrow [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro")'s communist government in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-7) which culminated in the failed [Bay of Pigs Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion "Bay of Pigs Invasion") in 1961, during which he declined to directly involve American troops.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-8) The following year, Kennedy de-escalated the [Cuban Missile Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis"), widely regarded as the closest that humanity has come to [nuclear holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_holocaust "Nuclear holocaust").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-9)

In 1963, Kennedy decided to travel to Texas to smooth over frictions within the [state's Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Democratic_Party "Texas Democratic Party") between liberal U.S. senator [Ralph Yarborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Yarborough "Ralph Yarborough") and conservative governor [John Connally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Connally "John Connally").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-11) The visit was first agreed upon by Kennedy, Johnson, and Connally during a meeting in [El Paso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso "El Paso") in June.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WarrenCommission-Page28-12) The motorcade route was finalized on November 18 and announced soon thereafter.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) Kennedy also viewed the Texas trip as an informal launch of his [1964 reelection campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_presidential_election "1964 United States presidential election").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-14)

Lee Harvey Oswald (born 1939)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-18) was a former [U.S. Marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Marine "U.S. Marine") who had served in Japan and the Philippines, and had espoused communist and socialist beliefs since reading [Karl Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Marx "Karl Marx") aged 14.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Philippines-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-21) After accidentally shooting his elbow with an unauthorized handgun and fighting an officer, Oswald was court-martialed twice and demoted.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Philippines-20) In September 1959, he received a [dependency discharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_discharge "Military discharge") after claiming his mother was disabled.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-22) A 19-year-old Oswald sailed on a freighter from [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") to France and then traveled to Finland, where he was issued a Soviet visa.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-23)

Oswald [defected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defection "Defection") to the Soviet Union,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-24)[[note 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-27) and in January 1960 he was sent to work at a factory in [Minsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minsk "Minsk"), Belarus.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-29) In 1961, he met and married [Marina Prusakova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marina_Oswald_Porter "Marina Oswald Porter"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-30) with whom he had a child.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Warren_1964,_p._712-31) In 1962, he returned to the United States with a repatriation loan from the U.S. embassy.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Warren_1964,_p._712-31) He settled in the [Dallas/Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex") area,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-32) where he socialized with Russian émigrés—notably [George de Mohrenschildt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_de_Mohrenschildt "George de Mohrenschildt"), a [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") informant.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-33)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-35) In March 1963, a bullet narrowly missed General [Edwin Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Walker "Edwin Walker") at his Dallas residence; a witness observed two conspicuous men. Relying on Marina's testimony, a note left by Oswald, and ballistic evidence, the [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission") attributed this assassination attempt to Oswald.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-36)

In April 1963, Oswald returned to his birthplace, New Orleans,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-37) and established an independent chapter of the pro-Castro [Fair Play for Cuba Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Play_for_Cuba_Committee "Fair Play for Cuba Committee"), of which he was the sole member.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-39) While passing out pro-Castro literature alongside unknown compatriots, Oswald was arrested after scuffling with anti-Castro [Cuban exiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_exiles "Cuban exiles").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-41)[[note 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-43) In late September 1963, Oswald traveled to [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), where, according to the Warren Commission, he visited the Soviet and Cuban embassies.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-44) On October 3, Oswald returned to Dallas and found work at the [Texas School Book Depository](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_School_Book_Depository "Texas School Book Depository") on [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WCR-C1-45) During the workweek he lived separately from Marina at [a Dallas rooming house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald_Rooming_House "Lee Harvey Oswald Rooming House").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Saturday2-46) On the morning of the assassination, he carried a long package (which he told coworkers contained curtain rods) into the depository;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-47)[[note 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-50) the Warren Commission concluded that this package contained Oswald's disassembled rifle.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-51)

## November 22

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of the John F. Kennedy assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_John_F._Kennedy_assassination "Timeline of the John F. Kennedy assassination").

### Kennedy's arrival in Dallas and route to Dealey Plaza

[![Image 10: Kennedy and the First Lady, dressed in a pink outfit and holding a bouquet, depart from Air Force One and greet the welcomers](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Kennedys_arrive_at_Dallas_11-22-63.JPG/250px-Kennedys_arrive_at_Dallas_11-22-63.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kennedys_arrive_at_Dallas_11-22-63.JPG)

President Kennedy and First Lady [Jacqueline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy_Onassis "Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis") arriving at [Dallas Love Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Love_Field "Dallas Love Field") on November 22, 1963

[![Image 11: The route of the motorcade: A right turn from Main Street onto Houston Street, then shortly thereafter a left turn before the Texas School Book Depository onto the snaking Elm Street, passing by the Grassy Knoll and exiting Dealey Plaza under the Triple Underpass bridge.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Dealey-plaza-annotated.png/330px-Dealey-plaza-annotated.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dealey-plaza-annotated.png)

The route of Kennedy's motorcade through [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza"). The shooting occurred on Elm Street.

On the evening of November 21, [Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_One "Air Force One") touched down in Fort Worth, Texas at 11:07 pm. The President and First Lady arrived at the [Hotel Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Texas "Hotel Texas") in downtown Fort Worth at 11:35 pm.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-:0-52)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-53) The following morning, November 22, President Kennedy and the First Lady boarded a [1961 Lincoln Continental convertible limousine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS-100-X "SS-100-X") to travel to a luncheon at the [Dallas Trade Mart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Trade_Mart "Dallas Trade Mart").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-odonnell-54)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) Other occupants of this vehicle—the second in the motorcade—were [Secret Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secret_Service "United States Secret Service") Agent [Bill Greer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Greer "William Greer"), who drove, Special Agent [Roy Kellerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Kellerman "Roy Kellerman") in the front passenger seat, and Governor Connally and his wife Nellie, who sat just forward of the Kennedys.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-55)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-56) Four Dallas police motorcycle officers accompanied the Kennedy limousine.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-57) Vice President Johnson, his wife [Lady Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Bird_Johnson "Lady Bird Johnson"), and Senator Yarborough rode in another convertible.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-58)

The motorcade's meandering 10-mile (16 km) route through Dallas was designed to give Kennedy maximum exposure to crowds by passing through a suburban section of Dallas,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-odonnell-54)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) and [Main Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Street_District,_Dallas "Main Street District, Dallas") in [Downtown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dallas "Downtown Dallas"), before turning right on Houston Street. After another block, the motorcade was to turn left onto Elm Street, pass through Dealey Plaza, and travel a short segment of the [Stemmons Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stemmons_Freeway "Stemmons Freeway") to the Trade Mart.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) The planned route had been reported in newspapers several days in advance.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) Despite concerns about hostile protestors—Kennedy's UN ambassador [Adlai Stevenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlai_Stevenson_II "Adlai Stevenson II") had been spat on in Dallas a month earlier—Kennedy was greeted warmly by enthusiastic crowds.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-59)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-60)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-61)

### Shooting
