[![Image 14: John F. Kennedy is fatally shot in the head, with Jacqueline Kennedy sitting beside him. Jacqueline can be seen turning over and looking at him at that moment.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Moorman_photo_of_JFK_assassination.jpg/250px-Moorman_photo_of_JFK_assassination.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Moorman_photo_of_JFK_assassination.jpg)

Robert Croft's photograph of Kennedy in [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza"), before the first shot struck Kennedy (_color photo_), and the [Mary Moorman photograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Moorman "Mary Moorman") (_b‍&‍w photo_), taken a fraction of a second after the fatal shot

Kennedy's limousine entered Dealey Plaza at 12:30 pm CST.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bugliosixi-3) Nellie Connally turned and commented to Kennedy, who was sitting behind her, "Mr. President, they can't make you believe now that there are not some in Dallas who love and appreciate you, can they?" Kennedy's reply—"No, they sure can't"⁠—were his last words.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-62)

From Houston Street, the limousine made the planned left turn onto Elm, passing the Texas School Book Depository.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-63) As it continued down Elm Street, multiple shots were fired: about 80% of the witnesses recalled hearing three shots.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Earwitnesses-64) The Warren Commission concluded that three shots were fired and noted that most witnesses recalled that the second and third shots were bunched together.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-65) Shortly after Kennedy began waving, some witnesses heard the first gunshot, but few in the crowd or motorcade reacted, many interpreting the sound as a firecracker or [backfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back-fire "Back-fire").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-66)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-67)[[note 5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-69)

[![Image 15: A straight line is shown illustrating the trajectory of the bullet that hit John F. Kennedy and John Connally, according to the single-bullet theory.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Sbt2.jpg/250px-Sbt2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sbt2.jpg)

[![Image 16: A curve showing the same bullet's trajectory in an alternative scenario where Kennedy sat directly behind Connally, according to conspiracy theorists.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Sbt_critics.jpg/250px-Sbt_critics.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sbt_critics.jpg)

Per the [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission")'s [single-bullet theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-bullet_theory "Single-bullet theory") (top), one bullet caused Kennedy's nonfatal wound and Connally's wounds. Conspiracy theorists, neglecting that Kennedy was not directly behind Connally, claim that the trajectory required a "magic bullet" (bottom).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-70)

Within one second of each other, Governor Connally and Mrs. Kennedy turned abruptly from their left to their right.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-71) Connally—an experienced hunter—immediately recognized the sound as that of a rifle and turned his head and torso rightward, noting nothing unusual behind him.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bugliosi39-68) He testified that he could not see Kennedy, so he started to turn forward again (turning from his right to his left), and that when his head was facing about 20 degrees left of center,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-johnconnally-72) he was struck in his upper right back by a shot he did not hear,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-johnconnally-72)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug61-73) then shouted, "My God. They're going to kill us all!"[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-74)

According to the Warren Commission and the HSCA, Kennedy was waving to the crowds on his right when a shot entered his upper back and exited his throat just beneath his [larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx "Larynx").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-75)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-76) He raised his elbows and clenched his fists in front of his face and neck, then leaned forward and leftward. Mrs. Kennedy, facing him, put her arms around him.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-johnconnally-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-aarclibrary.org-77)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-78) Although a serious wound, it likely would have been survivable.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-sabato216-79)

According to the Warren Commission's [single-bullet theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-bullet_theory "Single-bullet theory")—derided as the "magic bullet theory" by conspiracy theorists—Governor Connally was injured by the same bullet that exited Kennedy's neck. The bullet created an oval-shaped entry wound near Connally's shoulder, struck and destroyed several inches of his right fifth rib, and exited his chest just below his right nipple, [puncturing and collapsing his lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumothorax "Pneumothorax"). That same bullet then entered his arm just above his right wrist and shattered his right [radius bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius_(bone) "Radius (bone)"). The bullet exited just below the wrist at the inner side of his right palm and finally lodged in his left thigh.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-posnerbullet-80)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-81)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-sabato216-79)

[![Image 17: A sketch shows an arrow illustrating the first bullet that struck John F. Kennedy. The bullet is seen entering his neck and exiting his throat](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/HSCA-JFK-neck2-6-43.jpg/250px-HSCA-JFK-neck2-6-43.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HSCA-JFK-neck2-6-43.jpg)

[![Image 18: Another sketch shows an arrow illustrating the second bullet that fatally hit Kennedy in the head. Fragments are shown breaking from his skull.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/HSCA-JFK-head-7-125.jpg/250px-HSCA-JFK-head-7-125.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HSCA-JFK-head-7-125.jpg)

The trajectories of the two bullets that struck Kennedy, per the [House Select Committee on Assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Assassinations "United States House Select Committee on Assassinations")

As the limousine passed the [grassy knoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-haygood-82) Kennedy was struck a second time by a fatal shot to the head.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-83) The Warren Commission made no finding as to whether this was the second or third bullet fired, and concluded—as did the HSCA—that the second shot to strike Kennedy entered the rear of his head. It then passed in fragments through his skull, creating a large, "roughly [ovular](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/ovular "wikt:ovular")" [_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] hole on the rear, right side of the head, and spraying blood and fragments. His brain and blood spatter landed as far as the following Secret Service car and the motorcycle officers.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-84)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-85)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-86)[[note 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-88)

Secret Service agent [Clint Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Hill_(Secret_Service) "Clint Hill (Secret Service)") was riding on the [running board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_board "Running board") of the car immediately behind Kennedy's limousine.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-89) Hill testified to the Warren Commission that he heard one shot, jumped onto the street, and ran forward to board the limousine and protect Kennedy. Hill stated that he heard the fatal headshot as he reached the Lincoln, "approximately five seconds" after the first shot that he heard.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-cjhill-90) After the headshot, Mrs. Kennedy began climbing onto the limousine's trunk, but she later had no recollection of doing so.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-jacqueline-91) Hill believed she may have been reaching for a piece of Kennedy's skull.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-cjhill-90) He jumped onto the limousine's bumper, and he clung to the car as it exited Dealey Plaza and sped to [Parkland Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_Memorial_Hospital "Parkland Memorial Hospital"). After Mrs. Kennedy crawled back into her seat, both Governor and Mrs. Connally heard her repeatedly saying: "They have killed my husband. I have his brains in my hand."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-johnconnally-72)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-nellieconnally-92)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-93)

Bystander [James Tague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Tague "James Tague") received a minor wound to the cheek—either from a bullet or concrete curb fragments—while standing by the triple underpass.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-94) Nine months later, the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") removed the curb, and spectrographic analysis revealed metallic residue consistent with the lead core in Oswald's ammunition.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-newsweek_112814-95) Tague testified before the Warren Commission and initially stated that he was wounded by either the second or third shot of the three shots that he remembered hearing. When the commission counsel pressed him to be more specific, Tague testified that he was wounded by the second shot.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-96)

### Aftermath in Dealey Plaza

[![Image 19: Witness hunker down on the grassy incline before the grassy knoll after the shooting](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Newman_Family.jpg/330px-Newman_Family.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Newman_Family.jpg)

Civilians shielding their children after hearing shots and dropping to the grass. The grassy knoll and its picket fence are visible in the background.[[note 7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-98)

As the motorcade left Dealey Plaza, some witnesses sought cover,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-trask76-99) and others joined police officers to run up the grassy knoll in search of a shooter.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-haygood-82)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-100) No shooter was found behind the knoll's picket fence.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug852-101) Among the 178 witnesses who testified to the Warren Commission, 78 were unsure of the shots' origin, 49 believed they came from the depository, and 21 thought they came from the grassy knoll.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-102) No witness ever reported seeing anyone—with or without a gun—immediately behind the knoll's picket fence at the time of the shooting.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug852-101)

[Lee Bowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Bowers "Lee Bowers") was in a two-story [railroad switch tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switch_tower "Switch tower")120 yards (110 m) behind the grassy knoll's picket fence; he was watching the motorcade and had an unobstructed view of the only route by which a shooter could flee the grassy knoll; he saw no one leaving the scene.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug852-101) Bowers testified to the Warren Commission that "one or two" men were between him and the fence during the assassination: one was a familiar parking lot attendant, and the other wore a uniform like a county courthouse custodian. He testified seeing "some commotion" on the grassy knoll at the time of the assassination: "something out of the ordinary, a sort of milling around, but something occurred in this particular spot which was out of the ordinary, which attracted my eye for some reason which I could not identify".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-103)[[note 8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-105)

At 12:36 pm, teenager Amos Euins approached Dallas police sergeant D. V. Harkness to report having seen a "[colored man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colored "Colored") ... leaning out of the window [with] a rifle" on the sixth floor of the depository during the assassination; in response, Harkness radioed that he was sealing off the depository.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug80-106) Witness [Howard Brennan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Brennan "Howard Brennan") then approached a police inspector to report seeing a shooter—a white man in khaki clothing—in the same window.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-107)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-108) Police broadcast Brennan's description of the man at 12:45 pm.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-109) Brennan testified that, after the second shot, "This man... was aiming for his last shot... and maybe paused for another second as though to assure himself that he had hit his mark."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-110) Witness James R. Worrell Jr. also reported seeing a gun barrel emerge from a sixth-floor depository window.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-111) Bonnie Ray Williams, who was on the fifth floor of the depository, stated that the rifle's report was so loud and near that the ceiling plaster fell onto his head.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-112)

### Oswald's flight, murder of J. D. Tippit, and arrest

Further information: [John F. Kennedy assassination rifle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_rifle "John F. Kennedy assassination rifle") and [J. D. Tippit §Murder and investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._D._Tippit#Murder_and_investigation "J. D. Tippit")

[![Image 20: A photograph of the Texas School Book Depository, showing its view from a witness of John F. Kennedy's assassination. The window from the sixth floor is marked A, and another window from the fifth floor is marked B.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/HowardBrennan.jpg/250px-HowardBrennan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HowardBrennan.jpg)

[![Image 21: A view through a window to Elm Street, Dealey Plaza, from the shooter's location in the Depository to kill Kennedy, the so-called "sniper's nest".](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/View_from_Sniper%27s_nest_to_Elm_Street%2C_CE724.jpg/250px-View_from_Sniper%27s_nest_to_Elm_Street%2C_CE724.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:View_from_Sniper's_nest_to_Elm_Street,_CE724.jpg)

The view of the [Texas School Book Depository](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_School_Book_Depository "Texas School Book Depository") from witness [Howard Brennan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Brennan "Howard Brennan"): circle "A" indicates where he saw Oswald firing a rifle. At right, the view from the "sniper's nest" in the Texas School Book Depository.

When searching the sixth floor of the depository, two deputies found an Italian [Carcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcano "Carcano") M91/38 bolt-action rifle.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-113)[[note 9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-115) Oswald had purchased the used rifle the previous March under the alias "A. Hidell" and had it delivered to his Dallas [P.O. box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P.O._box "P.O. box").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-116) The FBI found Oswald's partial palm print on the barrel,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-117)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug801-118)[[note 10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-121) and fibers on the rifle were consistent with those of Oswald's shirt.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-122) A bullet found on Governor Connally's hospital [gurney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurney "Gurney") and two fragments found in the limousine were [ballistically matched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistic_fingerprinting "Ballistic fingerprinting") to the Carcano.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-123)

Oswald left the depository and traveled by bus to his boarding house, where he retrieved a jacket and revolver.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-124) At 1:12 pm, police officer [J. D. Tippit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._D._Tippit "J. D. Tippit") spotted Oswald walking in the residential neighborhood of [Oak Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Cliff "Oak Cliff") and called him to his patrol car. After an exchange of words, Tippit exited his vehicle; Oswald then shot Tippit three times in the chest. As Tippit lay on the ground, Oswald fired a final shot into Tippit's right [temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_(anatomy) "Temple (anatomy)"). Oswald then calmly walked away before running as witnesses emerged.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-125)

| Oswald speaking in custody |
| --- |
| [![Image 22: video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg)[Oswald professing innocence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ZYAIiErTNg) |
| [![Image 23: video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg)[Oswald's "press conference"](https://www.cbsnews.com/video/oswald-holds-press-conference/) |

As Dallas police officers conducted a roll call of depository employees, Oswald's supervisor, Roy Truly, realized that Oswald was absent and notified the police.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-126) Based on a false identification of Oswald, Dallas police raided a library in Oak Cliff before realizing their mistake.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-127) At 1:36 pm, the police were called after a conspicuous Oswald, tired from running, was seen sneaking into the [Texas Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Theatre "Texas Theatre") without paying.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-128) With the film _[War Is Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_Is\_Hell\_(film) "War Is Hell (film)")_ still playing, Dallas policemen arrested Oswald after a brief struggle in which Oswald drew his fully loaded gun.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-129) He denied shooting anyone and claimed he was being made a "[patsy](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/patsy#Noun "wikt:patsy")" because he had lived in the Soviet Union.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-130)

### Kennedy declared dead; Johnson sworn in

Main article: [First inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson "First inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson")

[![Image 24: Lyndon B. Johnson raises his hand above an outstretched Bible as he is sworn in as President as Air Force One prepares to depart Love Field in Dallas. Jacqueline Kennedy, still in her blood-spattered clothes (not visible), looks on.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Lyndon_B._Johnson_taking_the_oath_of_office%2C_November_1963.jpg/330px-Lyndon_B._Johnson_taking_the_oath_of_office%2C_November_1963.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lyndon_B._Johnson_taking_the_oath_of_office,_November_1963.jpg)

[Cecil W. Stoughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cecil_W._Stoughton "Cecil W. Stoughton")'s photograph of [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") being sworn in as President as [Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC-137C_SAM_26000 "VC-137C SAM 26000") prepares to depart Love Field in Dallas. [Jacqueline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy "Jacqueline Kennedy"), still in [her Chanel suit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_Chanel_suit_of_Jacqueline_Bouvier_Kennedy "Pink Chanel suit of Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy") (the blood spatters not visible here), looks on.

At 12:38 pm, Kennedy arrived in the emergency room of [Parkland Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_Memorial_Hospital "Parkland Memorial Hospital").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-131) Although Kennedy was still breathing after the shooting, his personal physician, [George Burkley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Burkley "George Burkley"), immediately saw that survival was impossible.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-132)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-hub-133)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-134) After Parkland surgeons performed futile [cardiac massage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_resuscitation "Cardiopulmonary resuscitation"), Kennedy was pronounced dead at 1:00 pm, 30 minutes after the shooting.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-hub-133) CBS host [Walter Cronkite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Cronkite "Walter Cronkite") broke the news on live television.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-135)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-136)

The Secret Service was concerned about the possibility of a larger plot and urged Johnson to leave Dallas and return to the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), but Johnson refused to do so without any proof of Kennedy's death.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-boyd-137)[[note 11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-139) Johnson returned to Air Force One around 1:30 p.m, and shortly thereafter, he received telephone calls from advisors [McGeorge Bundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGeorge_Bundy "McGeorge Bundy") and [Walter Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Jenkins "Walter Jenkins") advising him to depart for Washington, D.C., immediately.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Esquire;_September_16,_2013-140) He replied that he would not leave Dallas without Jacqueline Kennedy and that she would not leave without Kennedy's body.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-boyd-137)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Esquire;_September_16,_2013-140) According to _[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire\_(magazine) "Esquire (magazine)")_, Johnson did "not want to be remembered as an abandoner of beautiful widows".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Esquire;_September_16,_2013-140)

At the time of Kennedy's assassination, the murder of a president was not [under federal jurisdiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_crime_in_the_United_States "Federal crime in the United States").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-kurtz2-141) Accordingly, Dallas County medical examiner [Earl Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Rose_(coroner) "Earl Rose (coroner)") insisted that Texas law required him to perform an autopsy.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Munson-142)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Stafford-143) A heated exchange between Kennedy's aides and Dallas officials nearly erupted into a fistfight before the Texans yielded and allowed Kennedy's body to be transported to Air Force One.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Munson-142)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Stafford-143)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug110-144) At 2:38 pm, with Jacqueline Kennedy at his side, [Johnson was administered the oath of office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson "First inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson") by federal judge [Sarah Tilghman Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Tilghman_Hughes "Sarah Tilghman Hughes") aboard Air Force One, shortly before departing for Washington with Kennedy's coffin.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-145)

## Immediate aftermath

### Autopsy

Main article: [Autopsy of John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy_of_John_F._Kennedy "Autopsy of John F. Kennedy")

> Where bungled autopsies are concerned, President Kennedy's is the exemplar.

—Dr. [Michael Baden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Baden "Michael Baden"), chairman of the forensic pathology panel of the [House Select Committee on Assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Assassinations "United States House Select Committee on Assassinations")[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Bugliosi_2007_p._382-146)

President Kennedy's autopsy was performed at [Bethesda Naval Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Naval_Medical_Center "National Naval Medical Center") in [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland") on the night of November 22. Jacqueline Kennedy had selected a naval hospital as the postmortem site, as President Kennedy had been a [naval officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_officer "Naval officer") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-147)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-148) The autopsy was conducted by three physicians: naval commanders James Humes and J. Thornton Boswell, with assistance from ballistics wound expert Pierre A. Finck; Humes led the procedure.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-149) Under pressure from the Kennedy family and White House staffers to expedite the procedure, the physicians conducted a "rushed" and incomplete autopsy.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-150) Kennedy's personal physician, Rear Admiral George Burkley,[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-151) signed a [death certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_certificate "Death certificate") on November 23 and recorded that the [cause of death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cause_of_death "Cause of death") was a gunshot wound to the skull.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-amex-152)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-153)

Three years after the autopsy, Kennedy's brain—which had been removed and preserved for later analysis—was found to be missing when the Kennedy family transferred material to the [National Archives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Archives_and_Records_Administration "National Archives and Records Administration").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug431-154)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-brain-155) Conspiracy theorists often claim that the brain may have shown that the headshot entered from the front. Alternatively, the HSCA concluded that an assistant to Attorney General [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy"), the president's brother, likely removed the footlocker holding the brain and other materials at his direction, and he "either destroyed these materials or otherwise rendered them inaccessible" to prevent "misuse" of said material or to hide the extent of the [president's chronic illnesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy#Health "John F. Kennedy") and consequent medication.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug432-156)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-brain-155) Some autopsy X-rays and photographs have also been lost.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-157)

Most historians regard the autopsy as the "most botched" segment of the government's investigation.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Bugliosi_2007_p._382-146) The HSCA forensic pathology panel concluded that the autopsy had "extensive failings", including failure to take sufficient photographs, failure to determine the exact exit or entry point of the head bullet, not dissecting the back and neck, and neglecting to determine the angles of gunshot injuries relative to [body axis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_axis "Body axis").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-158) The panel further concluded that the two doctors were not qualified to have conducted a forensic autopsy. Panel member Milton Helpern—[Chief Medical Examiner for New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Chief_Medical_Examiner_of_the_City_of_New_York "Office of Chief Medical Examiner of the City of New York")—said that selecting Humes (who had only taken a single course on forensic pathology) to lead the autopsy was "like sending a seven-year-old boy who has taken three lessons on the violin over to the [New York Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Philharmonic "New York Philharmonic") and expecting him to perform a [Tchaikovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tchaikovsky "Tchaikovsky") symphony".[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-159)

### Funeral

Main articles: [State funeral of John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_funeral_of_John_F._Kennedy "State funeral of John F. Kennedy") and [List of dignitaries at the state funeral of John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_dignitaries_at_the_state_funeral_of_John_F._Kennedy "List of dignitaries at the state funeral of John F. Kennedy")

[![Image 25: Kennedy's coffin in front of the US Capitol](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/John_F._Kennedy_Lying_in_State_November_25%2C_1963_%2810965631824%29.jpg/250px-John_F._Kennedy_Lying_in_State_November_25%2C_1963_%2810965631824%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_F._Kennedy_Lying_in_State_November_25,_1963_(10965631824).jpg)

Kennedy's coffin is carried from the [Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol"), November 25

Following the autopsy, Kennedy lay in repose in the [East Room of the White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Room "East Room") for 24 hours.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-160)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-161) President Johnson issued [Presidential Proclamation 3561](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Proclamation%203561 "s:Proclamation 3561"), declaring November 25 to be a [national day of mourning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_day_of_mourning "National day of mourning"),[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-AssociatedPress-Page40-162)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-163) and that only essential emergency workers be at their posts.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-164) The coffin was then carried on a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Jack_(horse) "Black Jack (horse)")-drawn [caisson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limbers_and_caissons "Limbers and caissons") to the [Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol") to lie in state. Hundreds of thousands of mourners lined up to view the guarded casket,[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WhitePage16-165)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-166) with a quarter million passing through the [rotunda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Capitol_rotunda "United States Capitol rotunda") during the 18 hours of lying in state.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WhitePage16-165) Even in the Soviet Union, according to a memo by FBI director [J. Edgar Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Edgar_Hoover "J. Edgar Hoover")—news of the assassination "was greeted by great shock and consternation, and church bells were tolled in the memory of President Kennedy".[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-167)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-168)

Kennedy's funeral service was held on November 25, at [St. Matthew's Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_St._Matthew_the_Apostle_(Washington,_D.C.) "Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle (Washington, D.C.)"),[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WhitePage17-169) with the [Requiem Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Requiem_Mass "Requiem Mass") led by Cardinal [Richard Cushing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Cushing "Richard Cushing").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WhitePage17-169) About 1,200 guests, including representatives from over 90 countries, attended.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-170)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-nbc126-171) Although there was no formal eulogy,[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-172)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-173) Auxiliary Bishop [Philip M. Hannan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_M._Hannan "Philip M. Hannan") read excerpts from Kennedy's speeches and writings.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-nbc126-171) After the service, Kennedy was buried at [Arlington National Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery") in Virginia.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-174)[An eternal flame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Eternal_Flame "John F. Kennedy Eternal Flame") was lit at his burial site in 1967.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-175)

### Murder of Oswald

[![Image 26: Photograph of the moment Jack Ruby shot Oswald](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Ruby_shoots_Oswald.jpg/500px-Ruby_shoots_Oswald.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ruby_shoots_Oswald.jpg)

[Robert H. Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_H._Jackson_(photographer) "Robert H. Jackson (photographer)")'s photograph _[Jack Ruby Shoots Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_Ruby\_Shoots\_Lee\_Harvey\_Oswald "Jack Ruby Shoots Lee Harvey Oswald")_. Oswald was being escorted by police detective [Jim Leavelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Leavelle "Jim Leavelle") (tan suit) for the transfer from the city jail to the county jail. Ruby died in prison in 1967.

Further information: [Lee Harvey Oswald §Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald#Murder "Lee Harvey Oswald")

On Sunday, November 24, at 11:21 am, as Oswald was being escorted to a car in the basement of Dallas Police headquarters for the transfer from the city jail to the county jail, he was shot by Dallas nightclub owner [Jack Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ruby "Jack Ruby"). The shooting was broadcast live on television.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Saturday2-46)[Robert H. Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_H._Jackson_(photographer) "Robert H. Jackson (photographer)") of the _[Dallas Times Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas\_Times\_Herald "Dallas Times Herald")_ photographed the shooting; for the photograph, titled _[Jack Ruby Shoots Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_Ruby\_Shoots\_Lee\_Harvey\_Oswald "Jack Ruby Shoots Lee Harvey Oswald")_, he was awarded the 1964 [Pulitzer Prize for Photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulitzer_Prize_for_Photography "Pulitzer Prize for Photography").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-Fischer-176)

Drifting in and out of consciousness, Oswald was taken by ambulance to Parkland Memorial Hospital; he was treated by the same surgeons who had tried to save Kennedy.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-177) The bullet had entered his lower left chest but had not exited; major heart blood vessels such as the [aorta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aorta "Aorta") and [inferior vena cava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_vena_cava "Inferior vena cava") were severed, and the spleen, kidney, and liver were hit.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-178) Despite surgical intervention and [defibrillation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defibrillation "Defibrillation"), Oswald died at 1:07 pm.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-179)

Arrested immediately after the shooting, Ruby testified to the Warren Commission that he had been distraught by Kennedy's death and that killing Oswald would spare "Mrs. Kennedy the discomfiture of coming back to trial". He also stated he shot Oswald on the spur of the moment when the opportunity presented itself, without considering any reason for doing so.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-rubyWC-180) Initially, Ruby wished to represent himself in his trial until his lawyer [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli") dissuaded him: Belli argued that Ruby had an episode of [psychomotor epilepsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_lobe_epilepsy "Temporal lobe epilepsy") and was thus not responsible.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug357-181) Ruby was convicted, but the [decision was overturned on appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubenstein_v._State "Rubenstein v. State"). While awaiting retrial in 1967,[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-182) Ruby died of a [pulmonary embolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_embolism "Pulmonary embolism"), secondary to cancer. Like Oswald and Kennedy, Ruby was declared dead at Parkland Hospital.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-183)

## Films and photographs of the assassination

> My god, I saw the whole thing. I saw the man's brains come out of his head.

—[Abraham Zapruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Zapruder "Abraham Zapruder")[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-trask76-99)

[![Image 27: The Bell & Howell Zoomatic movie camera used by Abraham Zapruder](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Zaprudercamera.jpg/250px-Zaprudercamera.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zaprudercamera.jpg)

The [Bell & Howell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_&_Howell "Bell & Howell") Zoomatic movie camera used by [Abraham Zapruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Zapruder "Abraham Zapruder") to capture footage of the motorcade and Kennedy's killing, which later came to be known as the [Zapruder film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zapruder_film "Zapruder film"). The camera is preserved within the collection of the [National Archives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Archives_and_Records_Administration "National Archives and Records Administration").

Standing on the pergola wall some 65 feet (20 m) from the road,[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-184) tailor [Abraham Zapruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Zapruder "Abraham Zapruder") recorded Kennedy's killing on 26 seconds of silent [8 mm film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8_mm_film "8 mm film")—known as the [Zapruder film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zapruder_film "Zapruder film").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-lifezap-185) Frame 313 captures the exact moment at which Kennedy's head explodes.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-frenchies-186)_[Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_(magazine) "Life (magazine)")_ magazine published frame enlargements from the Zapruder film shortly after the assassination.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-lifezap-185)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-187) The footage itself was first publicly shown at the 1969 [trial of Clay Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Clay_Shaw "Trial of Clay Shaw"), and on television in 1975 by [Geraldo Rivera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldo_Rivera "Geraldo Rivera").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-188) In 1999, an arbitration panel ordered the federal government to pay $615,384 per second of film to Zapruder's heirs, valuing the complete film at $16 million (equivalent to $31.7 million in 2026).[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-189)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-190)

Zapruder was one of at least 32 people in Dealey Plaza known to have made film or still photographs at or around the time of the shooting.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-191) Most notably among the photographers, [Mary Moorman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Moorman "Mary Moorman") took several photos of Kennedy with her [Polaroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instant_camera "Instant camera"), including one of Kennedy less than one-sixth of a second after the headshot.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug885-192)

In addition to Zapruder, Charles Bronson, [Marie Muchmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Muchmore "Marie Muchmore"), and [Orville Nix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orville_Nix "Orville Nix") filmed the assassination, but at farther distances than Zapruder.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-193)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug452-194) Of the three, only Nix—who filmed the assassination from the opposite side of Elm Street from Zapruder, capturing the grassy knoll—actually recorded the fatal shot.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug452-194)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-nix-195)[[note 12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-196) In 1966, Nix claimed that, after he gave the film to the FBI, the duplicate that they returned had frames "missing" or "ruined". Although lower-quality duplicates exist, the original film has been missing since 1978.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-nix-195) Previously unknown footage filmed by George Jefferies was released in 2007.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-197)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-198) Recorded a few blocks before the shooting, the film captures Kennedy's bunched suit jacket, explaining the [discrepancies between the location of the bullet hole in Kennedy's back and his jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-bullet_theory#Location_of_back_wound "Single-bullet theory").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-199)

Some films and photographs captured an unidentified woman apparently filming the assassination; researchers have nicknamed her the [Babushka Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babushka_Lady "Babushka Lady") due to the [shawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headscarf "Headscarf") around her head.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-200) In 1978, [Gordon Arnold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Arnold "Gordon Arnold") came forward and claimed that he had filmed the assassination from the grassy knoll and that a police officer had confiscated his film.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-201) Arnold is not visible in any photographs taken of the area, which [Vincent Bugliosi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Bugliosi "Vincent Bugliosi")—author of _[Reclaiming History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reclaiming\_History "Reclaiming History")_—called "conclusive photographic proof that Arnold's story was fabricated".[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug887-202)

## Official investigations

### Dallas Police

[![Image 28: Oswald in police custody](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Lee_Harvey_Oswald_1963.jpg/250px-Lee_Harvey_Oswald_1963.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lee_Harvey_Oswald_1963.jpg)

[Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald") in police custody

At the Dallas Police headquarters, officers interrogated Oswald about the shootings of Kennedy and Tippit; these intermittent interviews lasted for approximately 12 hours between 2:30 pm on November 22 and 11 am on November 24.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-203) Throughout, Oswald denied any involvement and resorted to statements that were found to be false.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren180195-204)

Captain [J. W. Fritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._W._Fritz "J. W. Fritz") of the Homicide and Robbery Bureau did most of the questioning and kept only rudimentary notes.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-fritz-205)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-206) Days later, Fritz wrote a report of the interrogation from notes he made afterwards.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-fritz-205) There were no stenographic or tape recordings. Representatives of other law enforcement agencies were also present, including the FBI and the Secret Service, and occasionally participated in the questioning.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren180195-204) Several of the FBI agents who were present wrote contemporaneous reports of the interrogation.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-207)

On the evening of November 22, Dallas Police performed [paraffin tests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunshot_residue "Gunshot residue") on Oswald's hands and right cheek in an effort to establish whether or not he had recently fired a weapon. The results were positive for the hands and negative for the right cheek. Such tests were unreliable,[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren180195-204)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-208) and the Warren Commission did not rely on these results.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren180195-204)

The Dallas police forced Oswald to host a press conference after midnight on November 23, and, early in the investigation, made many leaks to the media. Their conduct angered Johnson, who instructed the FBI to tell them to "stop talking about the assassination".[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-kurtz2-141) Dallas Police, after the FBI expressed concerns that someone might try to kill Oswald, assured federal authorities that they would provide him adequate protection.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-209)

### FBI investigation

[![Image 29: Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy and President John F. Kennedy are pictured speaking at the White House](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Presentation_of_the_Young_American_Medals_for_Bravery._Attorney_General_Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Director_of_F.B.I._J...._-_NARA_-_194254.jpg/250px-Presentation_of_the_Young_American_Medals_for_Bravery._Attorney_General_Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Director_of_F.B.I._J...._-_NARA_-_194254.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Presentation_of_the_Young_American_Medals_for_Bravery._Attorney_General_Robert_F._Kennedy,_Director_of_F.B.I._J...._-_NARA_-_194254.jpg)

FBI Director [J. Edgar Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Edgar_Hoover "J. Edgar Hoover") (pictured between [Robert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy") and [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") in May 1963) wrote in a 1964 memo that "we left no stone unturned".[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug338-210)

The FBI immediately launched an investigation into the assassination, relying on a federal statute that forbade assaulting a federal officer. Within 24 hours of the killing, FBI Director Hoover sent President Johnson a preliminary report finding that Oswald was the sole culprit. After Ruby killed Oswald, Johnson decided that the Texas authorities were incompetent and instructed the FBI to conduct a complete investigation.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-kurtz2-141)

On December 9, 1963, the Warren Commission received the FBI's report of its investigation, which concluded that three bullets had been fired‍—‌the first striking Kennedy in the upper back, the second striking Connally, and the third striking Kennedy in the head, killing him.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-:2-211) The FBI continued to serve as the main investigative arm of the Warren Commission in the field. A total of 169 FBI agents worked on the case, conducting over 25,000 interviews and writing over 2,300 reports.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug338-210)

The thoroughness of the FBI's investigation is contested. Bugliosi applauded its quality and cites conspiracy theorist Harrison Edward Livingstone's praise of the FBI's commitment to following all leads.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-212) In its 1979 report, the HSCA found that the FBI's investigation of pro- and anti-Castro Cubans, and any connections to Oswald or Ruby, was insufficient.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bug338-210) The HSCA also noted that Hoover "seemed determined [to make the case that Oswald was the lone assassin] within 24 hours of the assassination".[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-213)

### Warren Commission

Main article: [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission")

[![Image 30: Members of the Warren Commission present their report to President Johnson](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/Warren_Commission_presenting_report_on_assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy_to_Lyndon_Johnson.jpg/500px-Warren_Commission_presenting_report_on_assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy_to_Lyndon_Johnson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lbj-wc.jpg)

The [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission") presents its report to President Johnson. From left to right: [John McCloy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._McCloy "John J. McCloy"), [J. Lee Rankin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Lee_Rankin "J. Lee Rankin") (General Counsel), Senator [Richard Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Russell,_Jr. "Richard Russell, Jr."), Congressman [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford"), Chief Justice [Earl Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Warren "Earl Warren"), President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson"), [Allen Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Dulles "Allen Dulles"), Senator [John Sherman Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sherman_Cooper "John Sherman Cooper"), and Congressman [Hale Boggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hale_Boggs "Hale Boggs")

On November 29, President Johnson established by executive order "[The President's Commission on the Assassination of President Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission")" and selected Chief Justice [Earl Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Warren "Earl Warren") of the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court") to chair the investigation, commonly known as the Warren Commission.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-214)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-kurtz2-141) Its 888-page final report was presented to Johnson on September 24, 1964, and made public three days later.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-215) It concluded that [Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald") had acted alone in killing Kennedy and wounding Connally, and that [Jack Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ruby "Jack Ruby") acted alone in killing Oswald.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-216)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-217) It made no conclusions as to Oswald's motive, but noted his [Marxism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxism "Marxism"), [anti-authoritarianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-authoritarianism "Anti-authoritarianism"), violent tendencies, failure to form personal relationships, and his desire to be significant in history.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-218)

Upon examining the Zapruder film, commission staffers realized that the FBI's gunshot theory was impossible. The reaction times of Kennedy and Connally were too close to have been caused by two bullets from Oswald: the reaction interval was less than the 2.3 seconds that it took to reload.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-219)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-220) This was one of the commission's most crucial findings: that a single shot caused the non-fatal wounds of Kennedy and Connally, known as the "single-bullet theory".[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-221)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-222) In May 1964, staffer [Arlen Specter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlen_Specter "Arlen Specter") replicated the single bullet's trajectory via a reenactment in Dealey Plaza: the bullet's path was exactly consistent with Kennedy's and Connally's wounds.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-223)

Out of the eight commission members, three—Representative [Hale Boggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hale_Boggs "Hale Boggs") and senators [John Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sherman_Cooper "John Sherman Cooper") and [Richard Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Russell_Jr. "Richard Russell Jr.")—found the theory "improbable"; their qualms were not mentioned in the final report.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-224) Conspiracy theorists labeled this theory the "magic bullet theory", partly due to the bullet's intact and purportedly pristine state. However, the HSCA's [Michael Baden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Baden "Michael Baden") noted that the bullet, despite its lack of fragmentation, was fundamentally deformed.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-posnerbullet-80) In 2023, Secret Service agent [Paul E. Landis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_E._Landis "Paul E. Landis")—who had stood on the running board of Kennedy's car—told _The New York Times_ that he retrieved the "magic bullet" from immediately behind Kennedy's seat upon arrival at Parkland, and that he placed it on Kennedy's stretcher. Landis believes that the bullet dislodged from a shallow wound in Kennedy's back.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-225)

As well as the Warren Report's 27 published volumes, the commission created hundreds of thousands of pages of investigative reports and documents. [Relman Morin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relman_Morin "Relman Morin") stated that "Never in history was a crime probed as intensely"; Bugliosi concluded that the commission's basic findings have "held up remarkably well".[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-226) According to [Gerald Posner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Posner "Gerald Posner"), the Warren report is "universally derided" by the American public.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-227) Walter Cronkite noted that "Although the Warren Commission had full power to conduct its own independent investigation, it permitted the FBI and the CIA to investigate themselves—and so cast a permanent shadow on the answers."[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-228) According to a 2014 report by CIA Chief Historian David Robarge, then-CIA director [John A. McCone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_A._McCone "John A. McCone") was involved in a "benign cover-up" by withholding information from the commission.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-229)

### Trial of Clay Shaw

Main article: [Trial of Clay Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Clay_Shaw "Trial of Clay Shaw")

On Friday, November 22, 1963, [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy"), the 35th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"), was [assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassinated "Assassinated") while riding in a presidential [motorcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorcade "Motorcade") through [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza") in [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), Texas. Kennedy was in the vehicle with First Lady [Jacqueline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy "Jacqueline Kennedy"), Texas governor [John Connally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Connally "John Connally"), and Connally's wife [Nellie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Connally "Nellie Connally"), when he was fatally shot from the nearby [Texas School Book Depository](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_School_Book_Depository "Texas School Book Depository") by [Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald"), a former [U.S. Marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). The motorcade rushed to [Parkland Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_Memorial_Hospital "Parkland Memorial Hospital"), where Kennedy was pronounced dead about 30 minutes after the shooting; Connally was also wounded in the attack but recovered. Vice President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") was [hastily sworn in as president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson "First inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson") two hours and eight minutes later aboard [Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_One "Air Force One") at [Dallas Love Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Love_Field "Dallas Love Field").

After the assassination, Oswald returned home to retrieve a pistol; he shot and killed a lone Dallas policeman [J. D. Tippit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._D._Tippit "J. D. Tippit") shortly afterwards. Around 70 minutes after Kennedy and Connally were shot, Oswald was apprehended by the [Dallas Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Police_Department "Dallas Police Department") and charged under Texas state law with the murders of Kennedy and Tippit. Two days later, as live television cameras covered Oswald being moved through the basement of [Dallas Police Headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Municipal_Building "Dallas Municipal Building"), he was fatally shot by Dallas nightclub operator [Jack Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Ruby "Jack Ruby"). Like Kennedy, Oswald was taken to Parkland Memorial Hospital, where he soon died. Ruby was convicted of Oswald's murder, though the decision was overturned on appeal, and Ruby died in prison in 1967 while awaiting a new trial.

After a 10-month investigation, the [Warren Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Commission "Warren Commission") concluded that Oswald assassinated Kennedy, and that there was no evidence that either Oswald or Ruby was [part of a conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_conspiracy_theories "John F. Kennedy assassination conspiracy theories"). In 1967, New Orleans district attorney [Jim Garrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Garrison "Jim Garrison") brought the only [trial for Kennedy's murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Clay_Shaw "Trial of Clay Shaw") against businessman [Clay Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Shaw "Clay Shaw"); Shaw was acquitted. Subsequent federal investigations—such as the [Rockefeller Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Commission "Rockefeller Commission") and [Church Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Committee "Church Committee")—agreed with the Warren Commission's general findings. In its 1979 report, the [United States House Select Committee on Assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Assassinations "United States House Select Committee on Assassinations") (HSCA) concluded that Kennedy was likely "assassinated as a result of a conspiracy". The HSCA did not identify possible conspirators, but concluded that there was "a high probability that two gunmen fired at [the] President". The HSCA's conclusions were largely based on a [police Dictabelt recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination_Dictabelt_recording "John F. Kennedy assassination Dictabelt recording"), which was subsequently debunked by the [U.S. Justice Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Justice_Department "U.S. Justice Department").

Kennedy's assassination is still the subject of widespread debate and has spawned many [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theories "Conspiracy theories") and alternative scenarios; polls have found that a vast majority of Americans believe there was a conspiracy. The assassination left a profound impact and was the first of four [major assassinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960s#Assassinations_and_attempts "1960s") during the [1960s in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960s_in_the_United_States "1960s in the United States"), coming two years before the [assassination of Malcolm X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Malcolm_X "Assassination of Malcolm X") in 1965, and five years before the assassinations of [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.") and Kennedy's brother [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Robert_F._Kennedy "Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy") in 1968. Kennedy was the fourth U.S. president to be assassinated and is the most recent to have [died in office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_who_died_in_office "List of presidents of the United States who died in office").

## Background

### Kennedy

Further information: [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") and [Presidency of John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy "Presidency of John F. Kennedy")

[![Image 7: President Kennedy is pictured speaking behind a podium. Rice University's stadium is visible behind him.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg/250px-John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_F._Kennedy_speaks_at_Rice_University.jpg)

[Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") delivering his "[We choose to go to the Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_choose_to_go_to_the_Moon "We choose to go to the Moon")" speech at [Rice University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_University "Rice University"), 1962

In 1960, John F. Kennedy, then a [U.S. senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"), was elected the 35th president of the United States with [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson") as his vice president.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-bugliosixi-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-4) Kennedy's tenure saw the height of the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and much of his foreign policy was dedicated to countering the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and [communism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-6) As president, he authorized operations to overthrow [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro")'s communist government in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-7) which culminated in the failed [Bay of Pigs Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion "Bay of Pigs Invasion") in 1961, during which he declined to directly involve American troops.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-8) The following year, Kennedy de-escalated the [Cuban Missile Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis"), widely regarded as the closest that humanity has come to [nuclear holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_holocaust "Nuclear holocaust").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-9)

In 1963, Kennedy decided to travel to Texas to smooth over frictions within the [state's Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Democratic_Party "Texas Democratic Party") between liberal U.S. senator [Ralph Yarborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Yarborough "Ralph Yarborough") and conservative governor [John Connally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Connally "John Connally").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-11) The visit was first agreed upon by Kennedy, Johnson, and Connally during a meeting in [El Paso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso "El Paso") in June.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-WarrenCommission-Page28-12) The motorcade route was finalized on November 18 and announced soon thereafter.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-warren40-13) Kennedy also viewed the Texas trip as an informal launch of his [1964 reelection campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_United_States_presidential_election "1964 United States presidential election").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_assassination#cite_note-14)

### Oswald

Main article: [Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald")

[![Image 8: Oswald is pictured passing out pamphlets on a street in New Orleans. Other men, possibly Cuban, are also passing out pamphlets behind him](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Pizzo_Exh_B-Oswald_leaflets_FPFC-WH_Vol21_139.jpg/250px-Pizzo_Exh_B-Oswald_leaflets_FPFC-WH_Vol21_139.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pizzo_Exh_B-Oswald_leaflets_FPFC-WH_Vol21_139.jpg)
