The constitution also sought to prevent Hutu or Tutsi hegemony over political power.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEconomist2003-167) Article 54 states that "political organizations are prohibited from basing themselves on race, ethnic group, tribe, clan, region, sex, religion or any other division which may give rise to discrimination".[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTECJCR2003article_54-168) According to [Human Rights Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Rights_Watch "Human Rights Watch"), this clause, along with later laws enacted by the parliament, effectively make Rwanda a [one-party state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_state "One-party state"), as "under the guise of preventing another genocide, the government displays a marked intolerance of the most basic forms of dissent".[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoth2009-169)

### Elections and referendum

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Kagame&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Elections and referendum")]

Since ascending to the presidency in 2000, Kagame has faced four [presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elections_in_Rwanda "Elections in Rwanda"), in 2003, 2010, 2017 and 2024. On each occasion, he was re-elected in a landslide, winning more than 90 percent of the vote.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEshadmin2017-170) A constitutional amendment referendum in 2015, which gave Kagame the ability to stand for additional terms, also passed by similar margins.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) International election monitors, human rights organisations and journalists generally regard these elections as lacking freedom and fairness, with interventions by the Rwandan state to ensure Kagame's victory.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTECaplan2018161-151)[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDepartment_of_State_(II)2017-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHuman_Rights_Watch_(IV)2017-173)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDeutsche_Welle2017-174) According to Ida Sawyer, Central Africa director for Human Rights Watch, "Rwandans who have dared raise their voices or challenge the status quo have been arrested, forcibly disappeared, or killed, independent media have been muzzled, and intimidation has silenced groups working on civil rights or free speech". Following the 2017 poll, Human Rights Watch released evidence of irregularities by election officials including forcing voters to write their votes in full view and casting votes for electors who had not appeared.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHuman_Rights_Watch_(IV)2017-173) The [United States Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") said it was "disturbed by irregularities observed during voting" as well as "long-standing concerns over the integrity of the vote-tabulation process".[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDepartment_of_State_(III)2017-175)

In their 2018 book _How to Rig an Election_, political scientists [Nic Cheeseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nic_Cheeseman "Nic Cheeseman") and [Brian Klaas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Klaas "Brian Klaas") said they were asked by journalists why Kagame went "through the motions of organizing a national poll that he was predestined to win". The book gave likely reasons for the continuation of the polls, including the fact that elections are "important to secure a base level of international legitimacy" and that "not even pretending to hold elections will get a country kicked out of the African Union".[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTECheesemanKlaas2018214%E2%80%93215-176) Law professor and human rights researcher Lars Waldorf wrote that the RPF's manipulation of polls could be designed to make itself appear stronger. Waldorf said that the party's margins of victory "are not meant to be convincing; rather, they are meant to signal to potential opponents and the populace that Kagame and the RPF are in full control."[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWaldorf201783-177) Scholars are divided on whether Kagame would have won the elections had he not used manipulative tactics. Writing about RPF intimidation of opposition candidates in the run-up to elections, Caplan said "what was most infuriating was that none of this was necessary for the RPF to hold on to power". Belgian academic [Filip Reyntjens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filip_Reyntjens "Filip Reyntjens") disagrees, however, stating that "the RPF is fully aware that opening up the political system would eventually lead to a loss of power".[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReyntjens2011-178)

#### Presidential election, 2003

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Kagame&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Presidential election, 2003")]

Main article: [2003 Rwandan presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Rwandan_presidential_election "2003 Rwandan presidential election")

The first post-genocide election was held in August 2003, following the adoption of the new constitution.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBBC_News_(VIII)2003-179) In May, the parliament voted to ban the [Republican Democratic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Democratic_Movement "Republican Democratic Movement") (MDR), following a parliamentary commission report accusing the MDR of "divisive" ideology.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIRIN_(II)2003-180) The MDR had been one of the coalition parties in the transitional government of national unity, and was the second-largest party in the country after the RPF.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBBC_News_(IX)2003-181)[Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") criticised this move, claiming that "the unfounded allegations against the individuals mentioned in the report appear to be part of a government-orchestrated crackdown on the political opposition".[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmnesty_International_(I)2003-182) Kagame was the RPF candidate, while former prime minister Twagiramungu was his main challenger. Twagiramungu had intended to run as the candidate for the MDR, but instead sought the presidency as an independent following the party's banishment.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIRIN_(III)2003-183) He returned to the country from Europe in June 2003 and began campaigning in August.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIRIN_(III)2003-183)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBBC_News_(X)2003-184)

Kagame declared victory in the election one day after the poll,[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBeaver_County_Times2003-185) and his win was later confirmed by the National Electoral Commission.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTENunley-186) The final results showed that Kagame received 95.1 per cent of the vote, Twagiramungu 3.6 per cent, and the third candidate, Jean Nepomuscene Nayinzira, 1.3 per cent; the voter turnout was 96.6 per cent.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTENunley-186) The campaign, election day, and aftermath were largely peaceful, although an observer from the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) raised concerns about intimidation of opposition supporters by the RPF.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReuters_(I)2003-187) Twagiramungu rejected the result of the election and also questioned the margin of victory, saying "Almost 100 per cent? That's not possible".[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReuters_(I)2003-187) He filed a petition at the Supreme Court to nullify the result, but was unsuccessful and he left Rwanda shortly afterwards, fearing that he would be arrested.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEIRIN_(IV)2003-188)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEImmigration_and_Refugee_Board_of_Canada2006-189) The EU observer also questioned the result, citing "numerous irregularities", but also describing the poll as a "positive step" in the country's history.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTECPJ2004-190)

#### Presidential election, 2010

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Kagame&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Presidential election, 2010")]

Main article: [2010 Rwandan presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rwandan_presidential_election "2010 Rwandan presidential election")

[![Image 13: Close up photo of Paul Kagame smiling at the premiere of the film Earth Made of Glass](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Paul_Kagame_New_York_2010.jpg/250px-Paul_Kagame_New_York_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paul_Kagame_New_York_2010.jpg)

Kagame in 2010

Kagame ran for re-election in 2010, at the end of his first elected term.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTECJCR2003articles_100%E2%80%93101-191)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoss2010-192) He was endorsed by the RPF national congress as their candidate in May 2010, and was accepted as a candidate in July.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKagireStraziuso2010-193) His highest-profile opponent was [Victoire Ingabire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoire_Ingabire "Victoire Ingabire"), a Hutu who had been living abroad for some years, and returned to Rwanda in January 2010 to run for the presidency.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKagireStraziuso2010-193) After a series of criticisms of Kagame's policies, she was arrested in April and prohibited from running in the election,[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhewell2010-194)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTENew_Times_(I)2010-195) as part of what Amnesty International's Tawanda Hondora described as "pre-electoral repression".[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-196) Kagame began his campaign with a rally at Kigali's [Amahoro Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amahoro_Stadium "Amahoro Stadium") on 20 July,[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-197) and held rallies across the country during the subsequent campaign period.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBraquehaisNorris-Trent2010-198) The rallies attracted tens of thousands, shouting enthusiastically for Kagame, although reporters for _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ interviewed a number of Rwandans who said that they were "not free to vote against him and that government officials down to the village level had put enormous pressure on them to register to vote; contribute some of their meager earnings to Mr. Kagame's campaign; and attend rallies".[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGettlemanKron2010-199)

The election went ahead in August 2010 without Ingabire and two other banned candidates, Kagame facing three opponents described by Human Rights Watch as "broadly supportive of the RPF".[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHuman_Rights_Watch_(II)2010-200) Kagame went on to receive 93.08 per cent of the vote in the election. Opposition and human rights groups said that the election was tainted by repression, murder, and lack of credible competition. Kagame responded by saying "I see no problems, but there are some people who choose to see problems where there are not."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAl_Jazeera_(II)2010-201)

#### Constitutional referendum, 2015

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Kagame&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Constitutional referendum, 2015")]

Main article: [2015 Rwandan constitutional referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Rwandan_constitutional_referendum "2015 Rwandan constitutional referendum")

As Kagame's second term progressed, he began to hint that he might seek to rewrite the term-limit clause of the Rwandan constitution, to allow him to run for a third term in the 2017 elections.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2014-202) Earlier in his presidency he had ruled it out,[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2014-202) but in a 2014 speech at [Tufts University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tufts_University "Tufts University") in the United States, Kagame said that he did not know when he would leave office, and that it was up to the Rwandan people to decide.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2014-202) He told delegates "...let's wait and see what happens as we go. Whatever will happen, we'll have an explanation."[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2014-202) The following year, a protest occurred outside [parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Rwanda "Parliament of Rwanda"),[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTELaing2015-203) and a petition signed by 3.7 million people—more than half of the electorate—was presented to lawmakers asking for Kagame to be allowed to stay in office.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAgence_France-Presse2015-204) The parliament responded by passing an amendment to the constitution in November 2015, with both the [Chamber of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_of_Deputies_of_Rwanda "Chamber of Deputies of Rwanda") and the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_Rwanda "Senate of Rwanda") voting unanimously in favour.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAl_Jazeera_(IV)2015-205) The motion passed kept the two-term limit in place, and also reduced the length of terms from 7 years to 5 years, but it made an explicit exception for Kagame, who would be permitted to run for a third 7-year term followed by two further 5-year terms, if he so desired.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAl_Jazeera_(IV)2015-205) After the amendment was passed in parliament, a referendum was required for it to come into effect.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAl_Jazeera_(IV)2015-205)

The referendum took place on 18 December 2015, with Rwandans overseas voting on 17 December.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBBC_News_(XVIII)2015-206) The amendment was approved by the electorate, with 6.16 million voters saying yes, approximately 98 per cent of the votes.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) The electoral commission stated that the vote had been peaceful and orderly.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) The [Democratic Green Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Green_Party_of_Rwanda "Democratic Green Party of Rwanda"), the most prominent domestic group opposing the change, protested that it had not been permitted to campaign openly against the amendment.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) Human Rights Watch executive director [Ken Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Roth "Ken Roth") announced on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that he did not believe the election to be free and fair, saying there was "no suspense in Rwanda referendum when so many dissidents silenced, civil society stifled".[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) The amendment itself was criticised by the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") and also the United States, which released a statement saying that Kagame should respect the previous term limits and "foster a new generation of leaders in Rwanda".[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171) Kagame responded that it was not his own decision to seek a third term, but that the parliament and the people had demanded it.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kagame#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcVeigh2015-171)

**Original Question:**
This African leader, born in the early 20th century visited the official residence of the leader of a global superpower in the 21st century. Apart from helping boost the economy of his country of origin, he also played a pivotal role in the restoration of peace in East Africa. This is a list of **foods and dishes named after people**.

## A

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Chicken_fettuccine_alfredo.JPG/250px-Chicken_fettuccine_alfredo.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chicken_fettuccine_alfredo.JPG)

[Fettuccine Alfredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fettuccine_Alfredo "Fettuccine Alfredo") with chicken (left)

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/Pommes_Anna.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pommes_Anna.jpg)

[Pommes Anna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pommes_Anna "Pommes Anna")

*   [Poularde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken "Chicken") Adelina Patti – named for 19th-century opera singer [Adelina Patti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelina_Patti "Adelina Patti").
*   [Woodcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodcock "Woodcock") salmis Agnès Sorel – one of the dishes [Agnès Sorel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agn%C3%A8s_Sorel "Agnès Sorel") (1422–1450) is reputed to have created herself. A garnish, soup, timbales, and tartlets all bear her name, as later chefs remembered her for her interest in food.
*   [Big Hearted Al](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith")[candy bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_bar "Candy bar") – early-20th-century presidential candidate [Al Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith") had this candy bar named after him by an admirer who owned a candy company. After Smith lost the presidential election of 1928 to Herbert Hoover, the candy bar was discontinued.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-1)
*   [Fillet of Beef Prince Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fillet_of_Beef_Prince_Albert "Fillet of Beef Prince Albert") – [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria")'s [Consort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Consort "Prince Consort")[Prince Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Albert_of_Saxe-Coburg_and_Gotha "Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha") (1819–1861). Also named for him: [Albert sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_sauce "Albert sauce") a [white sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_sauce "White sauce"), the [pea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pea "Pea") and [apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple "Apple") varieties, Coburg Soup (brussels sprouts and smoked bacon) and probably [Albert Pudding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Pudding?action=edit&redlink=1 "Albert Pudding (page does not exist)").
*   [Poularde Albufera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poularde_Albufera "Poularde Albufera"), [Albufera Sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albufera_Sauce "Albufera Sauce") – [Louis Gabriel Suchet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Gabriel_Suchet "Louis Gabriel Suchet") (1770–1826), one of [Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon")'s generals and Marshal of France for a time, was named duc d'Albufera after a lake near [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_(city_in_Spain) "Valencia (city in Spain)"), Spain, to mark his victory there during the [Peninsular War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsular_War "Peninsular War"). [Marie-Antoine Carême](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie-Antoine_Car%C3%AAme "Marie-Antoine Carême") created several dishes in the duke's honor, including duck, beef, and the sauce that accompanies this chicken.
*   [Alexandertorte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandertorte "Alexandertorte") – possibly Tsar [Alexander I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_I_of_Russia "Alexander I of Russia"), the gourmet Russian tsar who employed Antonin Carême. Finland claims the creation, allegedly by Swiss pastry chefs in Helsinki in 1818, in anticipation of the tsar's visit there.
*   [Gâteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A2teau "Gâteau") Alexandra – like her husband [Edward VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_VII "Edward VII"), [Alexandra of Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandra_of_Denmark "Alexandra of Denmark") (1844–1925) was honoured by an assortment of foods named after her when she was Princess of Wales and Queen. Besides this chocolate cake, there is consommé Alexandra, soup, sole, chicken quail, and various meat dishes.
*   [Lobster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobster "Lobster") Duke Alexis – the Russian [Grand-Duke Alexis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_III_of_Russia "Alexander III of Russia") made a highly publicized visit to the U.S. in 1871. A dinner for him at [Delmonico's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delmonico's "Delmonico's") featured this, and was kept on the menu by chef [Charles Ranhofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ranhofer "Charles Ranhofer").
*   [Fettuccine Alfredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fettuccine_Alfredo "Fettuccine Alfredo") – Alfredo di Lelio, an early-20th-century Italian chef invented the dish for his pregnant wife[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-Fox_News_2014-2) at his Roman restaurant and popularized it among tourists.
*   [Consommé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consomm%C3%A9 "Consommé") Princess Alice – this consommé with artichoke hearts and lettuce is named for [Princess Alice, Countess of Athlone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Alice,_Countess_of_Athlone "Princess Alice, Countess of Athlone") (1883–1981), one of [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria")'s granddaughters.
*   [Alice B. Toklas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_B._Toklas "Alice B. Toklas")' [hashish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashish "Hashish") fudge – due to the recipe being included in her book, _[The Alice B. Toklas Cook Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Alice\_B.\_Toklas\_Cook\_Book "The Alice B. Toklas Cook Book")_.
*   [Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%AAijoas_%C3%A0_Bulh%C3%A3o_Pato "Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato") – Portuguese poet, essay writer, memorialist, member of the Royal Academy of Sciences of Lisbon, renowned bon vivant and epicurean.
*   [Omelette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omelette "Omelette") André Theuriet – the French novelist and poet [André Theuriet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_Theuriet "André Theuriet") (1833–1907) has this omelette with truffles and asparagus named for him.
*   [Angelina Burdett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelina_Burdett?action=edit&redlink=1 "Angelina Burdett (page does not exist)")[plum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plum "Plum") – bred by a Mr. Dowling of Southampton, England around 1850, was named after the philanthropist Baroness [Angelina Burdett-Coutts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelina_Burdett-Coutts "Angelina Burdett-Coutts") (1814–1906).
*   [Pommes Anna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pommes_Anna "Pommes Anna") – the [casserole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casserole "Casserole") of sliced potatoes cooked in butter was created and named by French chef [Adolphe Dugléré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolphe_Dugl%C3%A9r%C3%A9 "Adolphe Dugléré") for the 19th-century courtesan/actress [Anna Deslions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Deslions "Anna Deslions"), who frequented Dugléré's [Café Anglais (Paris)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9_Anglais_(Paris) "Café Anglais (Paris)"). "Potatoes Annette" is a version of Potatoes Anna, with the potatoes julienned instead of in rounds.
*   [Arnold Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Palmer_(drink) "Arnold Palmer (drink)") – beverage of half lemonade and half iced-tea, named for the golfer, [Arnold Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Palmer "Arnold Palmer").
*   [Omelette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omelette "Omelette") Arnold Bennett – an unfolded omelette with smoked haddock invented at the [Savoy Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savoy_Hotel "Savoy Hotel") for the writer [Arnold Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnold_Bennett "Arnold Bennett")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-Skidelsky_2012-3)
*   [Oreiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_pie "Game pie") de la Belle Aurore – Claudine-Aurore Récamier, the mother of [Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Anthelme_Brillat-Savarin "Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin"), also has a lobster dish named after her but this elaborate [game pie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_pie "Game pie") was one of her son's favorite dishes. The large square pie contains a variety of game birds and their livers, veal, pork, truffles, aspic, and much else, in [puff pastry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puff_pastry "Puff pastry").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-4)
*   [Château Ausone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Ausone "Château Ausone")[red Bordeaux wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine "Bordeaux wine") – [Ausonius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ausonius "Ausonius") (310–395), the poet employed by [Valentinian I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentinian_I "Valentinian I") to tutor the Roman emperor's son, retired to the [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux") region and wrote about oyster farming. The wine named after him is said to be made of grapes grown on the site of his villa.

[Battenberg cake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battenberg_cake "Battenberg cake")

[Bing cherries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_cherry "Bing cherry")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/2_Eggs_Benedict.jpg/250px-2_Eggs_Benedict.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2_Eggs_Benedict.jpg)

[Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict")

*   [Bachwürfel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachw%C3%BCrfel "Bachwürfel") – a cubiform confectionery named after [Johann Sebastian Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach "Johann Sebastian Bach"), following the style of the [Mozartkugel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozartkugel "Mozartkugel").
*   [Baco noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baco_noir "Baco noir") – a hybrid grape, named after its breeder, [Maurice Baco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Baco "Maurice Baco").
*   [Baldwin apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldwin_apple "Baldwin apple") – Colonel [Loammi Baldwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loammi_Baldwin "Loammi Baldwin") (1745–1807), a commander of militia at the [Battle of Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lexington "Battle of Lexington"), found this apple between 1784 and 1793 while working as a surveyor and engineer on the Middlesex Canal in Massachusetts.
*   [Chicken Cardinal la Balue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_Cardinal_la_Balue?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chicken Cardinal la Balue (page does not exist)") – [Cardinal Jean la Balue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Jean_la_Balue "Cardinal Jean la Balue") (1421–1491), a somewhat notorious minister to [Louis XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XI "Louis XI"), is remembered in this dish of chicken, crayfish, and mashed potatoes.
*   [Barros Luco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barros_Luco "Barros Luco") – is a popular hot sandwich in Chile that includes beef and melted cheese in one of several types of bread. *   [Bartlett pear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartlett_pear "Bartlett pear") – The English [Williams pear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_pear "Williams pear") variety was inadvertently renamed by Massachusetts nurseryman [Enoch Bartlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enoch_Bartlett "Enoch Bartlett"), early 19th century. *   [Battenberg cake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battenberg_cake "Battenberg cake") – probably named after one of the late-19th-century princely [Battenberg family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battenberg_family "Battenberg family") living in England, who gave up their German titles during World War I and changed their name to [Mountbatten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountbatten "Mountbatten").
*   [Béarnaise sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9arnaise_sauce "Béarnaise sauce") – although often thought to indicate the region of Béarn, the sauce name may well originate in the nickname of French king [Henry IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_IV_of_France "Henry IV of France") (1553–1610), "le Grand Béarnais."
*   [Béchamel sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9chamel_sauce "Béchamel sauce") – named to flatter the maître d'Hotel to [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV "Louis XIV"), [Louis de Béchamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_de_B%C3%A9chamel "Louis de Béchamel"), Marquis de Nointel (1630–1703), also a financier and ambassador.
*   [Bellini (cocktail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellini_(cocktail) "Bellini (cocktail)") – [Giovanni Bellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Bellini "Giovanni Bellini")
*   [Ham mousseline à la Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ham_mousseline_%C3%A0_la_Belmont?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ham mousseline à la Belmont (page does not exist)") – [August Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_Belmont "August Belmont") (1816–1890) was born in Prussia and emigrated to the U.S. to work for the New York branch of Rothschild's. This dish was created at Delmonico's by Charles Ranhofer, probably for a dinner given there in Belmont's honor.
*   [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict") – at least two main accounts.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-Skidelsky_2012-3)[Lemuel Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemuel_Benedict?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lemuel Benedict (page does not exist)"), a New York stockbroker, claimed to have gone to the Waldorf Hotel for breakfast one day in 1894 while suffering a hangover.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-Fox_News_2014-2) He asked for a restorative in the form of toast, bacon, poached eggs, and [Hollandaise sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollandaise_sauce "Hollandaise sauce") on the side. The maître d' ([Oscar of the Waldorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Tschirky "Oscar Tschirky")) took an interest in Benedict's order, and adapted it for the Waldorf menu, substituting English muffins and ham, adding truffles, and naming it after Benedict. The other version: in 1893, [Charles Ranhofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ranhofer "Charles Ranhofer"), head chef of [Delmonico's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delmonico's "Delmonico's"), created the dish for Mr. and/or Mrs. [LeGrand Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeGrand_Benedict?action=edit&redlink=1 "LeGrand Benedict (page does not exist)"), New York stockbroker[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-Fox_News_2014-2) and socialite.
*   Eggs Benedict XVI – German-born [Pope Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") now has a Germanic version of the original [Eggs Benedict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Benedict "Eggs Benedict") named after him. Rye bread and sausage or sauerbraten replace the English muffins and Canadian bacon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-5)
*   Ben-Gurion's rice – folk name for [Israeli couscous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_couscous "Israeli couscous"), named for Israeli Prime Minister [David Ben-Gurion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ben-Gurion "David Ben-Gurion"), who spurred Eugen Proper, one of the founders of [Osem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osem_(company) "Osem (company)"), to devise a wheat-based substitute for rice.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_foods_named_after_people&printable=yes#cite_note-6)
*   [Eggs Berlioz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eggs_Berlioz?action=edit&redlink=1 "Eggs Berlioz (page does not exist)") – [Hector Berlioz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hector_Berlioz "Hector Berlioz") (1803–1869), the notable French composer, has his name on a dish of soft-boiled eggs, elevated by the addition of croustades, duchesse potatoes, and truffles and mushrooms in a Madeira sauce.
*   [Beyti kebab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyti_kebab "Beyti kebab") – [Beyti Güler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyti_G%C3%BCler?action=edit&redlink=1 "Beyti Güler (page does not exist)"), [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") restaurateur.

*   [Bing cherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_cherry "Bing cherry") – Oregon horticulturist [Seth Luelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Luelling "Seth Luelling") (or Lewelling) developed the cherry around 1875, with the help of his Manchurian foreman Bing, after whom he named it.
*   [Bintje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bintje "Bintje") – a very successful potato variety created by Dutch schoolteacher Kornelis Lieuwes De Vries who in 1905 named it after one of his pupils: the then 17 year old Bintje Jansma. *   [Boysenberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boysenberry "Boysenberry") – [Rudolf Boysen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Boysen "Rudolf Boysen"), botanist and Anaheim park superintendent, developed the loganberry/raspberry/blackberry cross around the 1920s. The berry was subsequently grown, named and marketed in the 1930s by [Walter Knott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Knott "Walter Knott") of [Knott's Berry Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knott's_Berry_Farm "Knott's Berry Farm") in California.
*   [Bramley apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bramley_apple "Bramley apple") – [Matthew Bramley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Bramley?action=edit&redlink=1 "Matthew Bramley (page does not exist)"), butcher who in 1846 bought a cottage in Southwell, Nottinghamshire, England, which had previously belonged to Mary Ann Brailsford, who had planted the first bramley tree there in 1809.
*   [Brillat-Savarin cheese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brillat-Savarin_cheese "Brillat-Savarin cheese") – [Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Anthelme_Brillat-Savarin "Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin") (1755–1826) has many dishes named for him besides this cheese, including partridge, eggs, garnishes, savory pastries, and the [Savarin cake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savarin_cake "Savarin cake"). Brillat-Savarin was the influential French author of _[The Physiology of Taste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Physiology\_of\_Taste "The Physiology of Taste")_, in which he advocated viewing cuisine as a science.
*   [Hot Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Brown "Hot Brown") – J. Graham Brown, owner of the [Brown Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_Hotel "Brown Hotel"), which first served the hot sandwich.
*   [Parson Brown orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_orange#Other_Valencias "Valencia orange") – Rev. Nathan L. Brown, 19th-century Florida minister and orange grower, developed what was to become the leading commercial orange of the time in the U.S.
*   [Burbank plum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prunus_'Climax' "Prunus 'Climax'") – [Luther Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luther_Burbank "Luther Burbank") (1849–1926), renowned American horticulturist, bred many new varieties of plants, including this and the [Russet Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russet_Burbank "Russet Burbank") potato.

Casimir-Perier was president for six months, until he resigned in 1895 under attacks from the leftist opposition party. *   [Charlotte Corday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Corday_(dessert)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Charlotte Corday (dessert) (page does not exist)") – [Charlotte Corday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Corday "Charlotte Corday") (1768–1793), the assassin of the radical [Jean-Paul Marat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Paul_Marat "Jean-Paul Marat") was paid tribute with an ice cream dessert by [Charles Ranhofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ranhofer "Charles Ranhofer") of [Delmonico's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delmonico's "Delmonico's").
*   [Charlotte Russe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Russe "Charlotte Russe") – a [dessert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dessert "Dessert") invented by the French [chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chef "Chef")[Marie-Antoine Carême](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie-Antoine_Car%C3%AAme "Marie-Antoine Carême") (1784–1833), who named it in honor of his Russian employer [Czar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czar "Czar")[Alexander I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_I_of_Russia "Alexander I of Russia") ("Russe" being the French equivalent of the adjective, "Russian"). *   [Chiboust cream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiboust_cream "Chiboust cream") – a cream filling invented by the French pastry chef [Chiboust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiboust?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chiboust (page does not exist)") in Paris around 1846, and intended to fill his [Gâteau Saint-Honoré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A2teau_Saint-Honor%C3%A9 "Gâteau Saint-Honoré"). *   [Choron sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choron_sauce "Choron sauce") – [Alexandre Étienne Choron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_%C3%89tienne_Choron "Alexandre Étienne Choron")

*   [Cobb salad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobb_salad "Cobb salad") – [Robert H. Cobb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_H._Cobb?action=edit&redlink=1 "Robert H.
